text:
Aj: Heads-up — I ran the new pacing + admit combo on the canary cluster for 6h. Posting quick notes and a few numbers.
Maria: Nice, curious about KV interaction. What were you tuning exactly?
Aj: Main change: prefer KV-hit requests in admission window. If queue has >= 70% KV-hit tokens, we allow slightly higher batch size target and relax token-budget per-request by +15%. The goal: exploit cheap KV hits to keep GPU batches full without raising tail latency.
Sahil: Interesting. How did you implement KV-priority? Is it strict head-of-line or scoring?
Aj: It's scoring. admission_score = base_score + alpha * kv_hit_ratio_in_queue. Requests sorted by score when forming batch window. alpha=0.8 in experiment.
Kevin: Any kernel fallback behavior coupled? We noticed earlier that larger batches trigger a different kernel which regresses for small seq lengths.
Aj: Yes, linked kernel selector: if batch token count > threshold we prefer wide-matmul kernel A, else kernel B. I bumped threshold from 2048 -> 3072 to allow the wider kernel only for truly large batches. Also added a safety check: if measured kernel latency for small-seq samples spikes > 20% we fallback to kernel B for next 2 minutes.
Eva: Can you share profiling numbers? Even rough percent changes help.
Aj: Sure — before: p95 latency (hosted canary) = 192ms. After KV-priority + alpha=0.8 + token-budget +15%: p95 = 182ms (-5.2%). p99 slightly worse: 420ms -> 438ms (+4.3%) — looks like a few requests hit the wider kernel and regressed.
Maria: p99 up is concerning. Is that because non-KV requests got pushed to final batches with big seqs and hit the slow kernel?
Aj: Exactly. Trace shows batches with mixed seq lengths where a handful long sequences forced kernel A and it doesn't handle short-seq well in our current fused ops.
Sahil: Any KV cache churn issues? If KV-hit ratio fluctuates, admission score will oscillate. Could cause jitter.
Aj: We observed short oscillations. To mitigate: added smoothing: kv_hit_ratio_smoothed = EMA(kv_hit_ratio, tau=10s). That reduced churn in admission order.
Kevin: What about soft-429 policy? Did you change reject thresholds?
Aj: Yes. Soft-limit now uses a two-tier heuristic: soft_admit_target_tokens and emergency_soft_cap. If queue_token_pressure > soft_target we soft-reject (reply 429 with Retry-After small), but only if the request score < score_threshold. For high-score (KV-heavy) we try to keep accepting until emergency_soft_cap.
Eva: Any user-facing impact observed? Errors or higher retry storms?
Aj: Small increase in 429s from 0.12% -> 0.27% during bursts, mostly for large non-KV requests. No retry storms yet — clients backoff fine. ci-bot: Perf test summary uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/1820012345.
Maria: The kernel regression needs more investigation. Could be quantization path or fused-op codegen. Did you capture GPU timelines?
Aj: Yes, collected CUPTI traces for the offending batches. Kernel A shows a 30% higher occupancy for short seqs, likely due to padding and memory layout.
Sahil: Quick experiment: could we pre-split mixed batches by seq-length buckets during formation? Keep buckets separate so kernel selector sees uniform seq-lengths.
Aj: I tried 1-hour run splitting into 3 buckets: short, mid, long. p99 improved to 405ms, p95 180ms. But throughput dropped ~2.3% because smaller buckets reduce packing efficiency.
Kevin: Tradeoff seems acceptable if p99 improves. Maybe combine with KV-priority: fill short-bucket with KV-hits first to keep efficiency.
Eva: Any perf regression after last quantized compile? That's our suspect.
Aj: We recompiled model B with int8 fast path a week ago; baseline perf before that was p99 398ms. After compile p99 420ms. The current canary shows 438ms when kernel A is used on short seqs.
Maria: So plan: 1) revert threshold bump -> reduce kernel A for mixed small batches 2) enable seq-length buckets + KV-priority within buckets 3) add kernel telemetry alert when kernel-specific p99 changes > 10% 4) keep soft-429 tuned to prefer dropping big non-KV during pressure.
Aj: Agree. I'll push a canary with buckets+kv-priority today and rollback threshold change.
Sahil: Also recommend we add an admission-mode flag per-customer so enterprise apps can opt into conservative admission (no soft relax).
Kevin: Good call. Ops: can you monitor retry rates and SLA errors after the canary?
Eva: I'll wire up dashboard panels for queue_token_pressure, kv_hit_ratio_smoothed, kernelA_p95/p99, and soft_429_rate.
ci-bot: Canary job started: canary-run-1820012345 (link: https://ci.internal/canary/1820012345).
Aj: Thanks all — will post a short follow-up with graphs and the CUPTI slices. If we see kernel A consistently bad on short seqs we should consider optimizing the kernel instead of routing around it.
Maria: SGTM. :thumbsup:
Sahil: Thanks — useful notes.
Kevin: +1
Eva: I'll watch the dashboard and ping if anomalies show up.
